clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old boy presented with a one-year history of recurrent fever, painful urination, increased frequency, and haematuria, with a history of recurrent UTIs treated with antibiotics. Initial workup was incomplete. An abdominal ultrasound revealed a left renal mass with multiple cystic lesions and a destroyed renal pelvis. A subsequent CT scan confirmed an enlarged left kidney with thinning cortices, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, calcifications, and parenchyma replaced with multiple septations, showing peripheral enhancement around non-enhancing cystic foci. Based on clinical presentation and imaging, a left radical nephrectomy was performed. Intra-operatively, an enlarged yellowish grey left kidney with mesenteric and hilar lymph nodes was observed, leading to radical left nephroureterectomy and hilar lymph node resection. Histological studies of the resected specimen showed gross yellowish renal tissues microscopically infiltrated with foamy lipid-laden macrophages, chronic inflammatory cells, and fibrosis, confirming Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The patient recovered well post-operatively and was discharged after a course of antibiotics.

The patient faired well postoperatively and was discharged home 10 days post nephrectomy.
